title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 9

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Which room will host the workshop?
tasks.audioText: The media studies tutor has moved the digital citizenship workshop to Room 26. It will start at nine forty-five on Tuesday. Students should review their public profile settings before the session and bring one example of an online post they would like to discuss. The workshop will include a short activity on how information can remain available after it is deleted.
options: Room 26
Room 16
Room 24
Room 28

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. What should students review before the session?
tasks.audioText: The media studies tutor has moved the digital citizenship workshop to Room 26. It will start at nine forty-five on Tuesday. Students should review their public profile settings before the session and bring one example of an online post they would like to discuss. The workshop will include a short activity on how information can remain available after it is deleted.
options: Their public profile settings
Their saved passwords
Their private messages
Their online shopping preferences

tasks.prompt: Before applying for a summer placement, Oleg reviewed the information visible on his public social media profile. He removed an old post that included a private timetable and changed the audience settings on several photographs. He also checked that his professional email address was suitable for applications. He understood that deleting a post could not guarantee that every copy had disappeared. Reading 1. What information did Oleg remove?
options: A photograph showing his home address
An old post containing a private timetable
A photograph showing his student card number
A comment about a college event

tasks.prompt: What did he understand about deleting a post?
options: Deleting a post removes every copy immediately
Deleting a post does not guarantee that every copy has disappeared
Only friends can save a copy of a post
Deleting a post guarantees that no one can save it.

tasks.prompt: Information posted online ___ available even after the original post is removed.
options: may remain
must remained
will remaining
is remain

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO sensible ways to manage a digital footprint.
options: Share your timetable publicly
Use the same public password everywhere
Review public profile settings
Think before posting personal information

tasks.prompt: The information about a person that remains visible through online activity is a digital ___.
A classmate wants to post a photograph showing another student's personal document. What should you say?
options: Post it quickly before anyone notices.
Please check that the document contains no private information and ask permission first.
It is fine because the photo is online.
Add more personal details to make it interesting.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of digital footprint in a logical order.
options: Change settings or remove unsuitable content
Review what information is publicly visible
Check the profile again before applying
Identify posts containing private details
correctOrder: Review what information is publicly visible
Change settings or remove unsuitable content
Check the profile again before applying

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how students can manage their digital footprint before applying for work placement.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the response identifies aspects of a digital footprint relevant to a work-placement application (0–2); it gives practical steps for reviewing or managing online content and privacy settings (0–2); advice is logically organised with understandable grammar (0–2); digital-reputation/privacy vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
